title: Short Stuff: Forest Lawn Memorial Park
summary: Short Stuff episode on Forest Lawn Memorial Park in Glendale, California. The hosts cover its founding in 1917 by Dr. Hubert Eaton (known as "the Builder"), his vision of a cemetery as a place to celebrate life with art, lawns, and fountains, and its comparisons to Walt Disney. They discuss the large Crucifixion painting by Jan Styka that the cemetery acquired and housed in a building, the replicas of Michelangelo's David (which has toppled several times), the themed burial sections such as Slumberland and Babyland, famous burials including Walt Disney, Elizabeth Taylor, Clark Gable, Bogart and Bacall, and Nat King Cole, and the fact that many weddings, including Ronald Reagan's first marriage to Jane Wyman, have taken place there. The episode also briefly compares Forest Lawn with Hollywood Forever Cemetery.

segments.title: Introduction and founding of Forest Lawn
segments.summary: The hosts introduce Forest Lawn Memorial Park in Glendale, its establishment in 1917 by Dr. Hubert Eaton, and Eaton's vision of a park-like cemetery where people celebrate life.

segments.title: Art, the Grand Tour, and the Crucifixion painting
segments.summary: Eaton wanted to give people a taste of European art locally. The hosts describe the Crucifixion painting by Jan Styka, which was left in the US and acquired by Forest Lawn, which built a building around it.

segments.title: Celebrity burials and Hollywood Forever
segments.summary: The hosts mention famous people buried at Forest Lawn and compare it with Hollywood Forever Cemetery, which hosts movie nights. Names listed include Elizabeth Taylor, Clark Gable, Bogart and Bacall, Nat King Cole, and Michael Jackson.

segments.title: Disney comparisons and themed burial sections
segments.summary: Eaton is often compared to Walt Disney, and Walt Disney is buried at Forest Lawn. The cemetery has themed sections such as Inspiration Slope, Whispering Pines, Dawn of Tomorrow, Babyland, and Slumberland.

segments.title: Cemetery walks, headstones, and naming ideas
segments.summary: The hosts discuss reading headstones on walks, noticing infant graves and World War Two veterans, and a writers' tip that cemeteries are a source of real names.

segments.title: David replica and weddings at Forest Lawn
segments.summary: A seventeen-foot replica of Michelangelo's David has toppled several times and was most recently knocked over under its own weight. The hosts then note that about sixty thousand weddings have taken place there, including Ronald Reagan's first marriage to Jane Wyman.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts joke about the statue and wedding facts, then close the Short Stuff episode with a standard sign-off and an iHeartRadio credit.
